final_answer:
**Short answer:** %CAR+ is the release CQA "CAR expression (% CAR+ of CD3+)", test code FC-CAR. Its PPQ performance is clean. Three gaps stand out:
- The vector freezer excursion (DEV-26-021) has no link to the vector lot it affected.
- Two verification records are stale or thin: the EMS escalation test and the FRZ-80-02 PQ.
- The time-to-transduction risk (FM-08) has no URS or test evidence.

One caveat on the first gap: the lot-level evidence for the excursion is circumstantial. It is a timing pattern, not a measured loss of titer.

## 1. Process parameters that drive %CAR+
The graph links three parameters to the attribute (INFLUENCES edges).

| Parameter | Criticality | Step | PPQ-001 criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| MOI | CPP | Transduction | Criterion 1: 4.0–6.0 TU/cell |
| Time from activation to transduction | CPP | Transduction | Criterion 5: 20–30 h |
| Vector storage temperature | KPP | Transduction (material handling) | None. PPQ does not evaluate it. |

Do not confuse FC-CAR with the day-5 in-process CAR value, which is an early read a few points lower.

## 2. Risks that threaten it
All four risks come from RA-PFMEA-001, the process FMEA for PV2.0.

| Risk | Failure mode | Sev/Occ/Det, RPN | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | MOI below target, from titer over-estimated or vector degradation | 8/4/4, 128 | HIGH |
| FM-07 | Vector held above -70 °C, so functional titer is lost | 8/2/6, 96 | HIGH |
| FM-08 | Transduction outside 20–30 h | 6/3/3, 54 | MEDIUM |
| FM-15 | Out-of-spec result not flagged, so a non-conforming lot is released | 10/2/4, 80 | HIGH |

FM-05 (MOI above target) affects VCN, not %CAR+.

## 3. Controls and test evidence, with gaps

| Risk | Controls (risk-linked) | Verification and evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | URS-EBR-007 (vector volume calculated from MOI and CoA titer), SOP-MFG-104 | CS-EBR-02 and TC-OQ-EBR-04 (scripted, tested 2.5–10 TU/cell). TX-0083 PASS on 2026-03-17. | Verified. Note that CC-26-022 would raise the target MOI to 8.0 (see section 6). |
| FM-07 | URS-ULT-001 (≤ -70 °C), URS-ULT-002 (high-temperature alarm), URS-EMS-014 (alarm escalation within 15 min), SOP-MAT-401 | **URS-ULT-001:** OQ test TC-OQ-ULT-01 passed on both freezers. It was re-run on FRZ-80-02 on 2026-04-24, after the compressor change CC-26-014. PQ test TC-PQ-ULT-01 passed on 2026-02-12 only, so **the PQ on FRZ-80-02 predates the compressor replacement and was not repeated**. **URS-ULT-002:** TC-OQ-ULT-02 passed, re-run on FRZ-80-02 after the change. **URS-EMS-014:** CS-EMS-03 and TC-OQ-EMS-04 passed on 2026-01-20 (TX-0070), but CC-26-011 changed CS-EMS-03 on 2026-03-16. | **URS-EMS-014: STALE**, because the last pass predates CC-26-011. That change control states "no re-testing required", but the stale rule applies regardless. The FRZ-80-02 PQ evidence is also stale. |
| FM-08 | SOP-MFG-104 and a batch-record timing check only | No URS, spec or test case is linked. | **Gap:** procedural control only, with no verification evidence. |
| FM-15 | URS-LIMS-003 (auto-flag out-of-spec results), URS-LIMS-002 (second-person review) | CS-LIMS-01 / TC-OQ-LIMS-03 (TX-0075) and CS-LIMS-02 / TC-OQ-LIMS-02 (TX-0074), both scripted and passed. | Verified. |

Notes on the table:
- The FRA risk rows (FRA-008, 009, 027, 031, 032, 040) rate all six linked URS items HIGH. Scripted testing is therefore required, and all of it is scripted.
- URS-EMS-014 matters in practice. During the FRZ-80-02 failure the alarm started at 03:20 and was acknowledged at 14:40, about 11 hours later (EV-26-0009).
- The PPQ protocol itself evaluates only MOI and time-to-transduction as drivers of %CAR+. Vector storage temperature and the QC flagging controls are not covered by any PPQ criterion.

## 4. How it is measured and validated
- **Method:** AM-FC-CAR, CAR expression by flow cytometry. Status is VALIDATED, with a validated range of 5–90 % of CD3+.
- **Validation:** protocol AMV-FC-CAR-01 (approved 2026-03-02, report approved). Test case TC-AMV-CAR-01 is scripted and tested 5–90 %. Execution TX-0086 passed on 2026-03-20.
- **Range check:** the PPQ results (36–45 %) sit inside the validated range.
- **Related method:** VCN per CAR+ cell is calculated from AM-VCN (ddPCR, validated 0.1–6.0, TX-0087 PASS) divided by FC-CAR.

## 5. PPQ performance (PPQ-001)
The criterion is ≥ 20 % CAR+ (criterion 8). The protocol status is "Execution complete – report pending".

| Batch | FC-CAR % | Result | MOI target | Hours to transduction | Vector lot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PPQ26-01 | 44.6 | PASS | 5.0 | 23.3 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-02 | 39.2 | PASS | 5.0 | 23.7 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-03 | 36.1 | PASS | 5.0 | 21.9 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-04 | 38.9 | PASS | 5.0 | 22.0 | LV26-021 |
| PPQ26-05 | 37.3 | PASS | 5.0 | 21.9 | LV26-021 |

- All five batches pass, and both CPPs stayed inside their ranges.
- VCN per CAR+ cell was 1.79–2.39, against a limit of ≤ 5.0.
- Both PPQ vector lots were stored in FRZ-80-01. The only excursion I found on that freezer (a defrost alarm on 2026-08-15) peaked at -78.6 °C, which is within limit.

## 6. Related deviations and what connects them

**DEV-26-021 → CAPA-26-008 → CC-26-014, on FRZ-80-02 (the vector freezer)**
- This is a major deviation. The compressor failed on 2026-04-20 and the chamber warmed to about -36 °C by the time the contents were moved at 15:30. The historian shows it later reaching -10 °C.
- The contents, including viral vector, were moved to FRZ-80-01.
- The impact assessment cites the supplier's ≤ -65 °C stability statement, concludes low risk, and places no lots on hold.
- CAPA-26-008 is closed and effective. The compressor was replaced under CC-26-014 and the OQ was partly re-run on 2026-04-24.
- The deviation is not linked to any material lot, so it has no AFFECTS link to LV25-118.

**DEV-26-027 → CAPA-26-016, low %CAR+ in ENG26-01 and ENG26-02**
- This is an atypical result and is still open. Its root cause is given as "donor variability, low CD3% at apheresis". CAPA-26-016 (open, due 2026-09-30) evaluates a minimum CD3% criterion.
- The data do not support that root cause.
  - Vector lot LV25-118 was in FRZ-80-02 during the excursion. It was transduced before the excursion in PD26-014 to PD26-023 (to 2026-04-15), with FC-CAR of 34.5–41.3 %.
  - After the excursion it was used in PD26-024 to PD26-027 and ENG26-01 to ENG26-03 (from 2026-04-22), with FC-CAR of 11.9–19.8 %.
  - Apheresis CD3 for ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 was about 64–65 %, which is not low.
  - MOI and transduction timing were normal throughout.
  - ENG26-03 shows the same low result but is not covered by the deviation.
  - Other lots stayed at about 38–45 % average.
- I would treat loss of LV25-118 titer from the excursion as the leading hypothesis. The CoA titer (1.04×10⁸ TU/mL) predates the excursion, so any lost potency would not show in uo04 or in the stated MOI.
- The material master still lists LV25-118 in FRZ-80-02, although the deviation says it was relocated.

**Other links**
- **DEV-26-033** is a protocol deviation against PPQ-001 (PPQ26-02 harvest viability, door latch). It does not involve %CAR+.
- **DEV-26-038** (PPQ26-04, label printer) and **DEV-26-041** (PPQ26-05, tubing leak, still open) are batch deviations that do not involve %CAR+.
- **CC-26-022** is open, at impact assessment. It would raise target MOI from 5.0 to 8.0 TU/cell to improve %CAR+, which is outside the PPQ-validated range of 4–6. SOP-MFG-104 is the only item it lists as impacted.
- **CC-26-004** (PV2.0, closed) updated RA-PFMEA-001.

**Recommended follow-ups**
1. Re-open the excursion assessment for vector lots LV25-118 and any cytokine lots that were in FRZ-80-02. Test titer and revisit the DEV-26-027 root cause and CAPA-26-016.
2. Re-execute TC-OQ-EMS-04 after CC-26-011.
3. Re-run the PQ on FRZ-80-02 after the compressor change.
4. Add verification evidence for the transduction timing control (FM-08).
5. Assess CC-26-022 against the PPQ range before approval.

content.text:
**Short answer:** %CAR+ is the release CQA "CAR expression (% CAR+ of CD3+)", test code FC-CAR. Its PPQ performance is clean. Three gaps stand out:
- The vector freezer excursion (DEV-26-021) has no link to the vector lot it affected.
- Two verification records are stale or thin: the EMS escalation test and the FRZ-80-02 PQ.
- The time-to-transduction risk (FM-08) has no URS or test evidence.

One caveat on the first gap: the lot-level evidence for the excursion is circumstantial. It is a timing pattern, not a measured loss of titer.

## 1. Process parameters that drive %CAR+
The graph links three parameters to the attribute (INFLUENCES edges).

| Parameter | Criticality | Step | PPQ-001 criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| MOI | CPP | Transduction | Criterion 1: 4.0–6.0 TU/cell |
| Time from activation to transduction | CPP | Transduction | Criterion 5: 20–30 h |
| Vector storage temperature | KPP | Transduction (material handling) | None. PPQ does not evaluate it. |

Do not confuse FC-CAR with the day-5 in-process CAR value, which is an early read a few points lower.

## 2. Risks that threaten it
All four risks come from RA-PFMEA-001, the process FMEA for PV2.0.

| Risk | Failure mode | Sev/Occ/Det, RPN | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | MOI below target, from titer over-estimated or vector degradation | 8/4/4, 128 | HIGH |
| FM-07 | Vector held above -70 °C, so functional titer is lost | 8/2/6, 96 | HIGH |
| FM-08 | Transduction outside 20–30 h | 6/3/3, 54 | MEDIUM |
| FM-15 | Out-of-spec result not flagged, so a non-conforming lot is released | 10/2/4, 80 | HIGH |

FM-05 (MOI above target) affects VCN, not %CAR+.

## 3. Controls and test evidence, with gaps

| Risk | Controls (risk-linked) | Verification and evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | URS-EBR-007 (vector volume calculated from MOI and CoA titer), SOP-MFG-104 | CS-EBR-02 and TC-OQ-EBR-04 (scripted, tested 2.5–10 TU/cell). TX-0083 PASS on 2026-03-17. | Verified. Note that CC-26-022 would raise the target MOI to 8.0 (see section 6). |
| FM-07 | URS-ULT-001 (≤ -70 °C), URS-ULT-002 (high-temperature alarm), URS-EMS-014 (alarm escalation within 15 min), SOP-MAT-401 | **URS-ULT-001:** OQ test TC-OQ-ULT-01 passed on both freezers. It was re-run on FRZ-80-02 on 2026-04-24, after the compressor change CC-26-014. PQ test TC-PQ-ULT-01 passed on 2026-02-12 only, so **the PQ on FRZ-80-02 predates the compressor replacement and was not repeated**. **URS-ULT-002:** TC-OQ-ULT-02 passed, re-run on FRZ-80-02 after the change. **URS-EMS-014:** CS-EMS-03 and TC-OQ-EMS-04 passed on 2026-01-20 (TX-0070), but CC-26-011 changed CS-EMS-03 on 2026-03-16. | **URS-EMS-014: STALE**, because the last pass predates CC-26-011. That change control states "no re-testing required", but the stale rule applies regardless. The FRZ-80-02 PQ evidence is also stale. |
| FM-08 | SOP-MFG-104 and a batch-record timing check only | No URS, spec or test case is linked. | **Gap:** procedural control only, with no verification evidence. |
| FM-15 | URS-LIMS-003 (auto-flag out-of-spec results), URS-LIMS-002 (second-person review) | CS-LIMS-01 / TC-OQ-LIMS-03 (TX-0075) and CS-LIMS-02 / TC-OQ-LIMS-02 (TX-0074), both scripted and passed. | Verified. |

Notes on the table:
- The FRA risk rows (FRA-008, 009, 027, 031, 032, 040) rate all six linked URS items HIGH. Scripted testing is therefore required, and all of it is scripted.
- URS-EMS-014 matters in practice. During the FRZ-80-02 failure the alarm started at 03:20 and was acknowledged at 14:40, about 11 hours later (EV-26-0009).
- The PPQ protocol itself evaluates only MOI and time-to-transduction as drivers of %CAR+. Vector storage temperature and the QC flagging controls are not covered by any PPQ criterion.

## 4. How it is measured and validated
- **Method:** AM-FC-CAR, CAR expression by flow cytometry. Status is VALIDATED, with a validated range of 5–90 % of CD3+.
- **Validation:** protocol AMV-FC-CAR-01 (approved 2026-03-02, report approved). Test case TC-AMV-CAR-01 is scripted and tested 5–90 %. Execution TX-0086 passed on 2026-03-20.
- **Range check:** the PPQ results (36–45 %) sit inside the validated range.
- **Related method:** VCN per CAR+ cell is calculated from AM-VCN (ddPCR, validated 0.1–6.0, TX-0087 PASS) divided by FC-CAR.

## 5. PPQ performance (PPQ-001)
The criterion is ≥ 20 % CAR+ (criterion 8). The protocol status is "Execution complete – report pending".

| Batch | FC-CAR % | Result | MOI target | Hours to transduction | Vector lot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PPQ26-01 | 44.6 | PASS | 5.0 | 23.3 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-02 | 39.2 | PASS | 5.0 | 23.7 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-03 | 36.1 | PASS | 5.0 | 21.9 | LV26-007 |
| PPQ26-04 | 38.9 | PASS | 5.0 | 22.0 | LV26-021 |
| PPQ26-05 | 37.3 | PASS | 5.0 | 21.9 | LV26-021 |

- All five batches pass, and both CPPs stayed inside their ranges.
- VCN per CAR+ cell was 1.79–2.39, against a limit of ≤ 5.0.
- Both PPQ vector lots were stored in FRZ-80-01. The only excursion I found on that freezer (a defrost alarm on 2026-08-15) peaked at -78.6 °C, which is within limit.

## 6. Related deviations and what connects them

**DEV-26-021 → CAPA-26-008 → CC-26-014, on FRZ-80-02 (the vector freezer)**
- This is a major deviation. The compressor failed on 2026-04-20 and the chamber warmed to about -36 °C by the time the contents were moved at 15:30. The historian shows it later reaching -10 °C.
- The contents, including viral vector, were moved to FRZ-80-01.
- The impact assessment cites the supplier's ≤ -65 °C stability statement, concludes low risk, and places no lots on hold.
- CAPA-26-008 is closed and effective. The compressor was replaced under CC-26-014 and the OQ was partly re-run on 2026-04-24.
- The deviation is not linked to any material lot, so it has no AFFECTS link to LV25-118.

**DEV-26-027 → CAPA-26-016, low %CAR+ in ENG26-01 and ENG26-02**
- This is an atypical result and is still open. Its root cause is given as "donor variability, low CD3% at apheresis". CAPA-26-016 (open, due 2026-09-30) evaluates a minimum CD3% criterion.
- The data do not support that root cause.

  - After the excursion it was used in PD26-024 to PD26-027 and ENG26-01 to ENG26-03 (from 2026-04-22), with FC-CAR of 11.9–19.8 %.
  - Apheresis CD3 for ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 was about 64–65 %, which is not low.
  - MOI and transduction timing were normal throughout.

  - Other lots stayed at about 38–45 % average.
- I would treat loss of LV25-118 titer from the excursion as the leading hypothesis. The CoA titer (1.04×10⁸ TU/mL) predates the excursion, so any lost potency would not show in uo04 or in the stated MOI.
